title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors — worked eigenvector problems
summary: Three class problems on finding eigenvalues and corresponding eigenvectors by the characteristic equation and row reduction; the third problem is only begun in the notebook.
transcription_policy: Notebook order and mathematical intent are preserved, with grammar lightly cleaned. Calculations were independently verified. Where the notebook contains a mathematical slip, the student-facing copy states the discrepancy explicitly rather than silently copying it.

items.final_answer: Eigenvalue \(8\) has eigenvector \([2\;-1\;1]^T\); the remaining eigenvalue is \(2\) with algebraic multiplicity 2.

blocks.text: The notebook briefly writes the roots as \(8,6,2\) and later starts a \(\lambda=6\) line. That is inconsistent with its own characteristic polynomial: \(\lambda=6\) is not a root. The correct roots are \(8,2,2\), so \(2\) is a repeated eigenvalue.

pages.heading: Example 4 — two independent eigenvectors for the repeated eigenvalue \(\lambda=2\)

blocks.text: The second and third rows are multiples of the first, so the equation reduces to
Thus the eigenspace for \(\lambda=2\) is two-dimensional. Two independent eigenvectors are \( [-1\;0\;2]^T \) and \( [1\;2\;0]^T \).
Together with the \(\lambda=8\) eigenvector \( [2\;-1\;1]^T \), this gives three linearly independent eigenvectors.

source_notes: The source consists of seven notebook photographs: Mac-class-unit2 - 5.jpg through Mac-class-unit2 - 11.jpg; raw notebook images are not copied into website assets.
The top of page 5 repeats the tail of the 8 September trace/transpose/inverse example. The dated 9 September entry begins at Example 3 below the written date, avoiding duplicate class-note content.
Example 3 was independently checked: eigenvalues are 0, 3 and 15, with corresponding eigenvectors proportional to [1,2,2]^T, [2,1,-2]^T and [2,-2,1]^T.
Example 4 contains a notebook slip: the characteristic polynomial factors as -(lambda-8)(lambda-2)^2, so the roots are 8, 2, 2 rather than 8, 6, 2. The student-facing copy records this explicitly.

Example 5 is incomplete in the supplied notes. The handwritten characteristic determinant also omits -lambda from the top-left diagonal entry; the correct setup is shown, but the solution is not invented.
